title: Thread `arg` and `call` through the `as_*()` S3 generics
description:
When closing #388, I stopped short of tackling this. If/when I resume this effort, this would be the next or final frontier.

When bad input reaches `as_dribble()`, `as_id()`, or `as_shared_drive()` from inside an exported function, the error reports the generic or an internal validator, not the user's function, and it doesn't name the offending argument:

```r
drive_ls(path = 1)
#> Error in `as_dribble()`:
#> ! Don't know how to coerce an object of class <numeric> into a <dribble>.

drive_get(id = "a@&")
#> Error in `validate_drive_id()`:
#> ...
```

Ideally these would read like ``Error in `drive_ls()`: `path` must be ...``.

Rough idea: methods take `arg = caller_arg(x), call = caller_env()` after `...` and forward them to the validators and the `.default` error, which could then use `stop_input_type()`. These defaults resolve to the generic's caller, so most call sites shouldn't need changing.

Open question: the `.character` and `.drive_id` methods go through `drive_get()`, so their errors will name `drive_get()` unless `call` is threaded through it as well.

title: Should ?drive_upload:overwrite mention drive_put?
description:
I am trying to write a script that saves a plot to drive; of course with plots, small tweaks are part & parcel of the job.

That means `drive_upload()` is probably inappropriate for my use case, though I'm accustomed to using it as my default go-to function so I'm most used to it.

Thus my journey to discovering `drive_put()`:

 1. Use `drive_upload()` [implicitly using the `overwrite=NA` default]. Oh crap, the re-run just created a new file with the same! Is there an `overwrite` parameter I should be using?
 2. Glance at `?drive_upload`. Yes! OK Let's try `overwrite=TRUE`.
 3. Looks good! Let's share this file. [Add the right permissions]. Oh crap, the re-run creates a new drive ID... which means the permissions I so painstakingly added were lost! Is that expected behavior?
 4. [Actually read `overwrite` carefully this time]. Oh, that's unfortunate... do I have to wait until the plot is finalized to set the permissions, then, to avoid this toil? That's unfortunate. Is it not possible to transfer the permissions over?
 5. [Check the Google Drive API... Check the {googledrive} issue tracker... Happen to see `drive_update()` mentioned for the first time] Oh, I guess I should be using `drive_update()`... but what about the initial upload? Oh, `?drive_update()` mentions `drive_put()`.

I've only just now noticed that `drive_put()` is mentioned at the top of `?drive_upload`, oops :)

All this to say, is there any downside to adding another mention of `drive_update()` and/or `drive_put()` under the description of `overwrite`?

https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/74a69a3a1fd66e930802ce6e461538c9e15f7c86/man-roxygen/overwrite.R#L8-L12

e.g.

> ...Note that the new file does not inherit any properties from the old one, such as sharing or publishing settings. It will have a new file ID. **If you need to keep permissions and the file ID, use [drive_update()] or [drive_put()].** An error is thrown if two or more pre-existing files are found.

title: Token becomes invalid after several uses
description:
I'm using non-interactive authorization to access google sheets with the following code:

```r
gs4_auth_configure(path = "path to .json")
options(
  gargle_oauth_cache = ".secret",
  gargle_oauth_email = "my email address"
)
gs4_auth(email = "my email address")

setwd("a different directory")
files <- list.files()

google_data <- read_sheet("sheet URL",
                          range = "SheetName!A:A",
                          col_types = "c")
```

I believe the first time I ran this, it actually required interactive authorization, but after that it always worked non-interactively. I copied the entire project folder over to a remote server, where it was happily running for several days before Friday 2/26/2021, when it resulted in the error:
```r
Error: Can't get Google credentials.
Are you running googlesheets4 in a non-interactive session? Consider:
  * `gs4_deauth()` to prevent the attempt to get credentials.
  * Call `gs4_auth()` directly with all necessary specifics.
See gargle's "Non-interactive auth" vignette for more details:
https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/non-interactive-auth.html
Execution halted
```

Going over to my local copy of the project, I get the error:
```r
Unable to refresh token: invalid_grant
Token has been expired or revoked. 
```

The only search result with that error is: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58296089/r-gmailr-how-to-re-establish-original-oauth-after-blastula-install-oath-overwrit

That person seems to have found the solution to be adding `gm_auth(cache=".secret")`, something my code already has.

I've done my best to heed the advice provided in the following links (and many more), to no avail:
https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/issues/239
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60507013/gmailr-without-selecting-a-pre-authorised-account-in-r
https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/non-interactive-auth.html
https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/get-api-credentials.html#service-account-token
https://googlesheets4.tidyverse.org/reference/index.html#section-auth

Did something happen last week that is causing this?

title: Legacy app documentation still online on the official website
description:
I suppose it's some sort of caching issue, but it's still kind of confusing, so here it goes.

On the official documentation website of `googledrive` this page is still online:
https://googledrive.tidyverse.org/articles/bring-your-own-app.html

If one looks carefully enough, it does appear that it relates to version 2.0, but if one clicks on the link to the home page, they get redirected to the home page of the documentation for version 2.1.1, so I suppose this is not intentional. 

How I encountered it in the real world:

1.  run an old script that relied on the `app` argument and get the error message:
>  "The `app` argument of `drive_auth_configure()` is deprecated as of googledrive 2.1.0."
2. put the error message in a search engine, and get link to this page among top results: https://googledrive.tidyverse.org/articles/bring-your-own-app.html - The domain looks good, and the title relevant to the issue I encounter
3. go through deprecated documentation before realising that it is actually deprecated 
4. finally, go the new website and go to what is the more relevant and updated page - https://googledrive.tidyverse.org/articles/bring-your-own-client.html

title: drive_find() does not always return exactly the same files
description:
The more difficult inverse problem addressed by e56b3f5d2e7b3a421115a1858df7456857478f5a. In that commit, I check for and  eliminate any results (file IDs) that appear in more than 1 page. But I fear the opposite can also happen: there can be files that appear in no page.

This is basically a re-opening of #277.

I have seen this myself now. It's hard to make a clean reprex, as the results are stochastic.

Summary: I can do `drive_find()` repeatedly and get a different number of files. Most recently, with my personal Google identity, I saw 972, 988, 988, and 988 files. (Note to self: In 3 out of 4 requests, I saw higher numbers reported in "Items so far", so the filter for duplicates is actually eliminating replicated IDs.)

The "missing" 988 - 972 = 16 files are a _subset_ of the 22 files in one specific folder.

I will attempt to create a clean example of this using curl alone (no R) and, if successful, report/ask upstream.

title: `drive_share` fails unexpectedly when sharing to certain users
description:
Function works for most users. Fails unexpectedly with certain users (2 out of 60). The file *does* end up being shared.

The error:

```
Caused by error in `map_chr()`:

```
referring to this line: https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/ed574d9eb3308619fc3e735251bfd42e6cfdb8e2/R/drive_share.R#L96

Apparently, the result of the previous line (`permission_out`) does not have the expected content.

I'm passing a 1-row `dribble`, to which I've added email and message columns. Constructing a reproducible example is difficult, because I'm not sure why these two dribbles are failing. They seem very similar to the rest of the rows, which do work. I could share a `dput` of the offending rows, but I'd want to be sure this is safe (not sharing sensitive user data).

This is what they look like, superficially

```

title: `drive_download()` error with KML mimeType
description:
There is a bug in `drive_download()` that causes it to fail on KML files depending on the mime type. KML mimeTypes are often `text/xml` or another raw text input. However, sometimes, depending on how they are loaded onto Drive, they are stored as `application/vnd.google-earth.kml+xml`.

Since `drive_download()` checks mimeType with `grepl("google", mime_type)`, KML files are mistakenly assumed to be a directly support mimeType by Google Drive and error is generated from `get_export_mime_type` since it isn't recognised as a mime type.

```r
#> Error in `get_export_mime_type()`:
#> ! Not a recognized Google MIME type:
#> ✖ application/vnd.google-earth.kml+xml
#> Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

I believe that this behavior is not ideal since downloading unsupported mime types should be okay, even if they aren't explicitly supported by the Google Drive API, since `get_export_mime_type()` is only checked if it appears to explicitly be a Google type. However, I may be wrong there.

Note that this code to check `mime_type` is also present in `drive_read()`.

title: Error downloading from team drive
description:
Dear Jenny and Lucy,

I am having difficulty downloading files from a team drive. I'm really going to struggle with a minimal reproducible example because of file confidentiality, but I've shared what I can below.

I have several small text files (`*.txt`) in a subfolder in a team drive, i.e.

- Datasets/keys/1234.txt
- Datasets/keys/5678.txt
etc

I am able to list these using:

```
keys = 
    googledrive::drive_ls(team_drive = dribble_team) %>% 
    filter(str_detect(name, ".txt$")) %>% 
    filter(str_detect(name, "^[0-9]....txt$"))
```

Where `dribble_team` is a `dribble` object linking to my team drive. The `keys` object is now a `dribble` in itself with the item `name`s, `id`s, and `drive_resource`s. 
When I try to download these items with `purrr::walk()` I get the following error:

```
walk(keys$id, googledrive::drive_download)
# Error: 'file' does not identify at least one Drive file.
```

Which I don't understand because `keys` is a dribble that contains info on several files. I've even checked by explicitly passing one known ID:

```
keys$id[1]
# [1] "0B-TotVDejb_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"

drive_download(file = keys$id[1])
# Error: 'file' does not identify at least one Drive file.
```

I can only think this is because this file exists on a team drive; I've been able to download from my own drive before.
I can't share these particular files but let me know if there's something that would be useful for you to replicate this problem and I'll do what I can.

Thanks.

title: Documentation request: Is drive_deauth the opposite of drive_auth?
description:
I am writing tests and would like a set/unset workflow like:

```r
test_that("", {
  set_auth(...)
  on.exit(unset_auth())
})
```

I _assume_ `drive_auth()` and `drive_deauth()` fit the bill, but was thrown a bit by the description in `?drive_deauth`:

> This can be used to access public resources for which no Google sign-in is required. This is handy for using googledrive in a non-interactive setting to make requests that do not require a token.

This makes it sound like they are more used for a different purpose, rather than for the flow I had in mind (re-setting state after a test). It would be helpful for the documentation to be more explicit here.

If they _are_ opposites, it might also be useful to offer a `withr`-esque pair of helpers useful for tests, i.e. `with_auth(...)` and `local_auth(...)`.

If they are _not_ opposites, it would be helpful to call this out in the documentation, and suggest alternatives / allude to why it may be difficult to un-set authorization in a given R session.

title: "Error: 'levels.drive_id()' not supported." when using apply on drive_ls() output
description:
Thank you very much for this great project. 

When using `apply` on the output of  `drive_ls()` with `googledrive` `2.0.0` from CRAN or this repo (e.g. to row-by-row create sub-folders and download the respective files) the error `Error: 'levels.drive_id()' not supported.` is thrown. With version `1.0.1`, it is possible to run `apply` on the output of `drive_ls()` without this error and without converting IDs to character.

See the reprex below orientated on the workflow that I have been using:

``` r
library(googledrive)
df <- drive_examples_remote() #or for me a `drive_ls()` call

# a download function using apply (here I usually create id-based subfolders etc.)
download_files <- function(df){
  catch <- apply(df, MARGIN = 1, function(x){
    drive_download(file = as_id(x[["id"]]), path = x[["name"]])
  })
}
```

Calling `download_files()` with `googledrive` `2.0.0` fails:

```r
# fails:
download_files(df[1:3,])
#> Error: `levels.drive_id()` not supported.

rlang::last_error()
#> <error/vctrs_error_unsupported>
#> `levels.drive_id()` not supported.
#> Backtrace:
#>  1. global::download_files(df[1:3, ])
#>  2. base::apply(...)
#>  4. base::as.matrix.data.frame(X)
#>  6. vctrs:::levels.vctrs_vctr(xj)
#>  7. vctrs:::stop_unsupported(x, "levels")
#>  8. vctrs:::stop_vctrs(...)
#> Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see the full context.
```
Calling `apply` on a `drive_ls()` output works with  `googledrive` `1.0.1` or by converting the IDs to character and removing the `drive_resource` column:

```r
df$drive_resource <- NULL
df$id <- as.character(df$id)
download_files(df[1:2,])
#> File downloaded:
#> • 'chicken_doc' <id: 1X9pd4nOjl33zDFfTjw-_eFL7Qb9_g6VfVFDp1PPae94>
#> Saved locally as:

Could it be that there is a method missing for class `"drive_id"  "vctrs_vctr" "character"`? 

Its not so problematic for me since I simply can convert to character but maybe it would be convenient if `apply` would work directly.

Thanks!

title: `drive_upload()` fails when "vctrs_vctr" class is cached as a child of "list"
description:
Code to reproduce:

```r
library(posterior) # (>= 1.3.0)
library(googledrive)

# posterior makes "vctrs_vctr" be cached as a child of "list"
getClassDef("vctrs_vctr") 
#> Virtual Class "vctrs_vctr" [package "posterior"]
#> 
#> Slots:
#>             
#> Name:  .Data
#> Class:  list
#> 
#> Extends: 
#> Class "list", from data part
#> Class "vector", by class "list", distance 2
#> 
#> Known Subclasses: "rvar"

gd_id <- as_id("<some GD folder URL>")
class(gd_id)
#> [1] "drive_id"   "vctrs_vctr" "character"

drive_example_local("chicken.jpg") %>%
  drive_upload(
    name = "name-squatter",
    path = gd_id,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
#> Error: C stack usage  7954920 is too close to the limit
```

I was able to find out that this happens because `drive_upload()` [at some point](https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/c7325dfcf1da648ad4764e7f6c6e5e2fc6a5d593/R/drive_upload.R#L135) needs to write a list, one of which elements is a drive id, to json. If you run `jsonlite:::asJSON(gd_id)`, you'll get the same C stack error.

An output of `as_id()` has the following classes: `c("drive_id",  "vctrs_vctr", "character")`. So I think this is what happens:

1. `asJSON` doesn't have a method for "drive_id" and "drive_id" is not extended by any other class (`extends("drive_id")`), so it applies the "ANY" method. See `selectMethod(jsonlite:::asJSON, "drive_id")`.
2. This method basically just [strips away the first class of the object](https://github.com/jeroen/jsonlite/blob/13e48ded961666495a6dbeaf4ceff1ff0f3dbb31/R/asJSON.ANY.R#L13) and leaves `c("vctrs_vctr", "character")`.
3. Then R searches for a `asJSON` method for "vctrs_vctr" and because it is extended by "list" (because of `posterior` loaded), applies the list method. See `selectMethod(jsonlite:::asJSON, "vctrs_vctr")`.
4. The "list" method traps into endless recursion [here](https://github.com/jeroen/jsonlite/blob/13e48ded961666495a6dbeaf4ceff1ff0f3dbb31/R/asJSON.list.R#L35) when it tries to `vapply()` `asJSON()` to the object because `x[[1]]` is identical to `x`.

I can't really tell whether it's something that `jsonlite` should've handled, or it's `posterior` doing something wrong. But I think regardless it's a matter of a simple update to prevent this from happening in `googledrive`?  
- drive id can be explicitly converted to character before being passed to `toJSON` in `drive_upload()`
- or "drive_id" class can be defined as a child of "character". If I run `setClass("drive_id", contains = "character")` at the beginning of the session, I don't get the error.

title: Provide workflows for the "missing functions"
description:
There are certain things we don't do right now. And might not ever. These are things that Drive does not directly support but that are possible by composing several operations. We should reveal the workflow, using the functions googledrive has, in an article:

  * Copy a Drive folder, recursively. Demo for at least a simple folder that contains only files. 
  * Upload a local folder, recursively. See also #25 for some discussion.
  * ~~List a Drive folder, **recursively**.~~ *done by `drive_ls()` now*
  * A general pattern for mapping functions that are not vectorized. Example: doing `drive_ls()` for a vector of folders.
  * *more to come*

*Update: many of these are less interesting now that `drive_ls()` supports recursion. But will leave this open as a place to collect workflows to incorporate into the website.*

title: Expand upon "Download failed"?
description:
Hi,

Thanks for a very useful package. For reasons I do not fully understand, I experience from time to time download errors when using `googledrive` to download data from some of my R packages, i.e.

`Error in googledrive::drive_download(): ! Download failed.`

I suspect it has to do with some download limitations by the Google Drive API, but I am not sure.

Would it be possible to utilize more information regarding the [request made](https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/main/R/drive_download.R#L103-L107), so that the user is somewhat better informed regarding the reason for why the download in fact failed? 

kind regards,
Sigve

title: Expose a method for downloading a large file via "exportLinks"
description:
Similar to https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/2357 and 
 https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/2243

Problem - when a file is too large (5mb or 10mb depending on output and input), you may get an error like:
```
        "reason": "exportSizeLimitExceeded",
        "message": "This file is too large to be exported."
```

Here's an example slide deck I used https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1XdwxvjgZivWsgLLpR-Hi9F_d3RKqeIRWF2rFcAv3Gic/edit#slide=id.p


``` r
library(googledrive)
id = as_id("1XdwxvjgZivWsgLLpR-Hi9F_d3RKqeIRWF2rFcAv3Gic")
tfile = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
get_result = drive_get(id)
#> Using an auto-discovered, cached token.
#> To suppress this message, modify your code or options to clearly consent to the use of a cached token.
#> See gargle's "Non-interactive auth" vignette for more details:
#> https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/non-interactive-auth.html
#> The googledrive package is using a cached token for muschellij2@gmail.com.
dl = drive_download(id, path = tfile,
                    overwrite = TRUE, type = "pdf")
#> Error: The file doesn't seem to have downloaded.
# file exists though
file.exists(tfile)
#> [1] TRUE
file.size(tfile)
#> [1] 238
```

# Add in function

``` r
download_wrapper = function(id, path, type, verbose = TRUE) {
  ttype = toupper(type)
  dl = try({
    googledrive::drive_download(
      id,
      path = path,
      overwrite = TRUE,
      type = type)
  }, silent = TRUE)
  
  if (inherits(dl, "try-error")) {
    message("File was too large for drive_download, using export link")
    get_result = googledrive::drive_get(id)
    if (nrow(get_result) < 1) {
      stop(paste0(ttype, " could not be downloaded"))
    }
    if (nrow(get_result) > 1) {
      warning("Multiple files detected - picking the first")
    }
    url = get_result$drive_resource[[1]]$exportLinks
    mime_ext = googledrive::drive_mime_type(type)
    url = url[[mime_ext]]
    if (!is.null(url)) {
      out = httr::GET(
        url,
        httr::write_disk(path, overwrite = TRUE),
        if (verbose) httr::progress())
      if (httr::status_code(out) >= 400) {
        stop(paste0(ttype, " could not be downloaded"))
      }
    } else {
      stop(paste0(ttype, " could not be downloaded"))
    }
  }
  return(dl)
}

title: Resource key may be necessary to access certain shared files
description:
Just a head's up: a security fix for Google Drive URLs will be rolled out in Sept 2021.

<https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2021/07/heres-what-that-google-drive-security-update-message-means/>

> Google's new link scheme adds a "resourcekey" to the end of any shared Drive links, making them harder to guess. So a link that used to look like "https://drive.google.com/file/d/0BxI1YpjkbX0OZ0prTHYyQ1U2djQ/" will now look like "https://drive.google.com/file/d/0BxI1YpjkbX0OZ0prTHYyQ1U2djQ/view?resourcekey=0-OsOHHiQFk1QEw6vIyh8v_w." The resource key makes it harder to guess.

I'm not sure exactly what updates need to be made to `googledrive` to account for this change.

title: Make Files Read-Only on Google Drive via RStudio
description:
[Google Drive API v3](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/reference/files/update) allows us to update a file's metadata/content. The "contentRestrictions[].reason" property under [Request Body](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/reference/files/update#request-body) makes the content of a file read-only. I have explored ways to implement this request in R but could not seem to successfully lock the file's content.

```r
test <- shared_drive_get("test_drive")
test_upload <- drive_upload("test_file", path=test)

# I first tried to use a named parameter to pass along to the Drive API
test_upload <- test_upload %>%
  drive_update(contentRestrictions[].readOnly=TRUE)
# Received output "Error: unexpected symbol in:"

# I also tried to use "request_generate" but could not find the corresponding endpoint.
fileId <- "1e8L2QX_NDbxuQ2DPxH97Tdyd6Owy1CK7"
lockfile <- request_generate(
  endpoint = "ContentRestriction",
  list(fileId = fileId),
  token = drive_token()
  )

```

title: Drives resource collection is replacing Team Drives collection
description:
Email received 2019-04-24

---

Hello G Suite Developer,

We are writing to let you know that we are making changes to Drive API, Drive Activity API and Google Picker API and we identified your app(s) as being impacted.

On April 24, 2019, we introduced a new Drive API resource collection, called Drives, to replace the Team Drives resource collection. The Drives resource collection can help you create, delete, get, list and update your shared drives. It features all the same fields, resources and available methods as the Team Drives resource collection.

Starting June 1, 2020 all related Team Drives fields for Drive API, Drive Activity API and Google Picker API, will be deprecated. Consider migrating and updating your app(s) to the Drives resource collection as soon as possible. Please see the migration guide for further details.

Additionally, starting June 1, 2020, applications will no longer be able to opt-in to support shared drives. This means that shared drive items (including both shared drives and files within shared drives) will be returned in all relevant requests, if applicable for a given user.

If you have additional questions or need assistance, please visit this page.

Sincerely,

The G Suite Team

---

title: drive_upload overwrite does not work when type is set
description:
Thank you for developing and maintaining library(googledrive). I ran into the following problem with drive_upload.

```r
library(googledrive)
write.csv(mtcars,'mtcars.csv',row.names = F)
drive_upload(media = 'mtcars.csv',type = 'spreadsheet',overwrite = T)
```

title: Save a token to be used instead of prompting the user to use a pre authorized account or obtain a new token
description:
I'm tring to source a R script into another R script, the original script accesses a list of files using the drive_ls function and then downloads the latest file using the drive_download function

The script works fine without any interruption when ran using my local machine, but while I try to run it using a remote desktop its always throws the following prompt "The googledrive package is requesting access to your Google account. Select a pre-authorised account or enter '0' to obtain a new token. Press Esc/Ctrl + C to abort."

I'm wanting to have this script run using the task scheduler so that I don't need to have any sort of human intervention

Another part of my script accesses the googlesheets4 package and even it throws the same prompt while using the read_sheet function

Is there a way to save the token of an account that I've already authorized and load it to the environment to get rid of this prompt ?

title: Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) :    gnutls_handshake() failed: An unexpected TLS packet was received.
description:
Hello, thanks for this awesome package!

I've been trying to automate `drive_download()` to download many files. Everything seems to work fine, but occasionally I get the error message "Auto-refreshing stale OAuth token." followed by the more cryptic error message in the title. Rerunning `drive_auth()` before relaunching tasks doesn't seem to work, as soon as I execute `drive_find()` or `drive_download()` the error reappears.  The only workaround I've found is to manually restart the r session and start from scratch, which is not ideal for automation. 

Do you have any clue how I could fix this without terminating R? It would be great if I could just wrap everything in a tryCatch to keep things chugging along instead of halting entirely... 

I've stripped down the code to bare bones, and assume you have a few "chicken" files to download in order to make this a true reprex:
```r
# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(googledrive)
library(purrr)

# get a dribble of chicken files, convert each dribble row to element of a list
dribble_chicken_list <- drive_find(pattern = "chicken") %>%
   rowwise()  %>%
   group_split()

# map through list
map_df(.x = dribble_chicken_list,
           ~drive_download(file = .x, path = "./"))

#> File downloaded:
#>   * chicken_1
#> Saved locally as:
#>   * chicken_1
# (... chicken_n)
#> Auto-refreshing stale OAuth token.
#> Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : 
#    gnutls_handshake() failed: An unexpected TLS packet was received. 
```

title: Unable to authorize from Rstudio Server
description:
From Rstudio Server, I downloaded the package, ran `drive_search()`, and proceeding through the authorization process, which resulted in an error:

```
This site can't be reached; localhost refused to connect.
```
There's a nice [tutorial ](https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/217952868-Generating-OAuth-tokens-from-a-server) on how to overcome this problem by manually generating a token with the out of band option set to `TRUE`.

This worked for me:

```r
library(googledrive)
options(httr_oob_default=TRUE) 
drive_auth(new_user = TRUE) 

#> No token currently in force.
#>Please point your browser to the following url: 

#>  https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/...
```

It was not immediately obvious to me that the problem was related to the fact that I was running R in a server. Please consider adding this to the package's documentation to save future users the head scratching and googling.

Thanks for the great package - I'm looking forward to testing it out!

title: Utility to immediately provide shareable link to data
description:
I've been using the following for a little while to quickly share small datasets via Google Drive.

Would love to submit a PR, not sure about the best final form for this:

```r
# upload a data frame to google drive, make it shareable, and
# copy the shareable link into the clipboard
get_shareable_link_to_data <- function(data, path, direct = TRUE) {
  readr::write_csv(data, path)
  df <- googledrive::drive_upload(path, path)
  df <- googledrive::drive_share(df, role = "reader", type = "anyone")

  if (direct)
    link <- paste0("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=", df$id)
  else
    link <- googledrive::drive_link(df)

  clipr::write_clip(link)
  fs::file_delete(path)
  cat(link)
  invisible(link)
}
```

When `direct = TRUE`, the link can be immediately used in `read_csv()`. When `direct = FALSE`, the link send users to the Google Drive preview of the data.

title: Cannot download shared file
description:
I am the maintainer of the ropensci/onekp package. This package is a portal to public data that was previously available though FTP, but now it is on a shared Google Drive. When I try to download these files with `curl`, Google directs me to a page that requires confirmation to bypass the virus scan (ropensci/onekp#2).

As an alternative to directly using `curl`, I have been trying to download the files with `googledrive` using the UUIDs. But this fails:

```r
library(googledrive)
googleID <- as_id("1GrB19Tl87zAbpqh3wgO8NCi9xR371MZq")
x <- drive_get(googleID)
x
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   name             id                                drive_resource
#> * <chr>            <chr>                             <list>        
#> 1 URDJ.faa.tar.bz2 1GrB19Tl87zAbpqh3wgO8NCi9xR371MZq <list [37]> 
drive_download(x)
#> Error: The file doesn't seem to have downloaded.
```

The metadata retrieved by `drive_get` looks correct (`x$drive_resource[[1]]`), for example it finds the correct name of the dataset maintainer.

The downloaded file (`URDJ.faa.tar.bz2`) has the following content:

```
{
 "error": {
  "code": 500,
  "message": null
 }
}
```

It seems that `drive_get` can find the public file, but that `drive_download` cannot. Is downloading download external shared files not supported?

title: Rework args of `drive_mkdir()`
description:
Current pattern in related functions:

``` r
drive_cp <-       function(file,  path = NULL, name = NULL)
drive_mv <-       function(file,  path = NULL, name = NULL)
drive_upload <-   function(media, path = NULL, name = NULL)
drive_mkdir <-    function(       path = NULL, name = NULL)
```

which I think of as FUNCTION(SOMETHING, PATH, NAME).

Currently `drive_mkdir()` has no SOMETHING. But the name of the new folder should be SOMETHING and we don't need NAME. This will make the calls more natural and can still be seen as consistent with the other functions.

title: BioC_mirrors.csv not found
description:
The examples in the "Upload files" section of the googledrive website (http://googledrive.tidyverse.org/#upload-files) uses the `BioC_mirrors.csv` file as an example, e.g. 

    (mirrors <- drive_upload(R.home('doc/BioC_mirrors.csv'), "README-mirrors.csv"))

For my R installation on Ubuntu 14.04, `R.home('doc/BioC_mirrors.csv')` returns `"/usr/lib/R/doc/BioC_mirrors.csv"`, yet there is no such file. However using

    `file.path(R.home("doc"), "BioC_mirrors.csv")`

as in `utils::chooseBioCmirror` returns `"/usr/share/R/doc/BioC_mirrors.csv"` which does exist, so specifying the file this way would fix this issue for me and presumably is a more general solution as that is what `utils::chooseBioCmirror` uses.

Note the path is used twice in this section.

title: drive_download() return local file path as new column in returned dribble
description:
I'd like to suggest that the dribble returned form `drive_download()` contain a column or field in drive_resource which maps the remote file to the local path. 

For files that you might have some automated post processing for this would be amazingly handy (e.g. pandoc'ing).

Also useful for batch update with `drive_update()`.

P.S. I am pretty excited about what might be possible with this package. Amazing work! :+1: :star:

description: @LucyMcGowan How do you examine current sharing status? Seems like we don't have a nice workflow for that.

title: Naming pattern for functions that reveal details
description:
We need to do something to unify functions that show you the current state of files in a dribble wrt trashed-ness, path, sharing status, publishing status, etc.

Should it be:

`drive_show_trash()`
`drive_show_path()`
`drive_show_sharing()`
`drive_show_publish()`

title: Consistent policy re: duplicate names
description:
In some functions, we don't let you create a file "foo" if "foo" already exists. Examples:

  * *I think `drive_upload()`?*

In others, we silently let this happen:

  * `drive_mkdir()`

In googlesheets, I've always thrown a warning or message, when people do this, so they know they have >1 file with the same name.

We need to take a position on this and be consistent everywhere.

title: Deleting multiple files at once
description: Noticed while preparing demo: what if you have several dribbles lying around and you want to delete them all? It's cumbersome to delete one by one. Think on this.

title: drive_add_path() doesn't seem to recognize multiple parents if one is My Drive
description:
I noticed this while working on adding metadata to `drive_upload()`. Since we haven't merged that in, I'll write an example using `drive_update()`. I believe this is due to [checking if the file is in root and if so returning only the root folder](https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/master/R/drive_add_path.R#L50), but have written out an example to remind myself later.

```
## Upload a file into 'My Drive'
x <- drive_upload(system.file("DESCRIPTION"))

## Create 2nd parent folder
y <- drive_mkdir("folder")
x <- drive_update(x, addParents = y$id)

drive_add_path(x)
#>  # A tibble: 1 x 4
#>          name          path                           id files_resource
#> *       <chr>         <chr>                        <chr>         <list>
#> 1 DESCRIPTION ~/DESCRIPTION 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTMHFZbW5nSUpWM0k    <list [37]>

x$files_resource[[1]]$parents
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "0B0Gh-SuuA2nTZ01sNTl0dGRaTXM"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "0AEGh-SuuA2nTUk9PVA"
```

If the file has 2 parents that AREN'T 'My Drive' all seems to be 👌 

```
y <- drive_mkdir("folder1")
z <- drive_mkdir("folder2")

## Upload a file into 'folder1'
x <- drive_upload(system.file("DESCRIPTION"), path = y)

## Add z
x <- drive_update(x, addParents = z$id)
drive_add_path(x)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>         name                  path                           id files_resource
#> *       <chr>                 <chr>                        <chr>         <list>
#> 1 DESCRIPTION ~/folder2/DESCRIPTION 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTemphbk5HRmtlUUk    <list [37]>
#> 2 DESCRIPTION ~/folder1/DESCRIPTION 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTemphbk5HRmtlUUk    <list [37]>
```

title: Consider exporting promote()
description:
No.

But we should have a workflow article (#123) that shows how to dig, e.g. `mimeType` or `owner`, out of the metadata.

title: Team Drives
description:
We have basically decided to NOT pass parameters through willy nilly in our high level functions. But we have to provide a global way to accommodate files on Team drives. I would prefer to think about having some default query params that are sent automatically for relevant endpoints + a way to manipulate them vs. putting `...` everywhere.

https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/web/enable-teamdrives

Good news:

> If your application isn't affected by the behavioral differences, then you only need to include the `supportsTeamDrives=true` query parameter in requests. This is an acknowledgement that the application is aware of behavioral differences of files contained in Team Drives.

Bad news:

`files.list` endpoint obviously has some special considerations re: Team Drives. Ditto for permissions.

title: drive_upload() and metadata
description: Once #158 is done, we should revisit `drive_upload()`. It should probably have greater capabilities re: metadata.

title: Revisit default fields for the Files resource
description:
If you set custom files fields in, say, `drive_search()` and do NOT include `"kind"`, then `as_dribble.list()` fails. Either we should always force `"kind"` to be included in the requested fields or stop requiring it and only require name and id.

Dilemma: it's nice to be able to control the fields (for speed) but it's hard to predict what you want to do downstream. If you don't get the right fields, those calls will fail. Maybe we need to try harder to find a minimal set of fields used by high-level googledrive functions and make it hard to form high-level requests that don't include at least these?

We error here because "kind" is not included.

```r
drive_search(fields = prep_fields(c("name", "id", "starred")))
#> Traversing pages . .
#>  Show Traceback
#>  
#>  Rerun with Debug
#>  Error: purrr::map_lgl(x, ~all(required_nms %in% names(.x))) are not all TRUE 
```

This call technically succeeds:

```r
drive_search(fields = prep_fields(c("name", "id", "starred", "kind")))
```

but it would be interesting to determine which downstream functions will fail due to lack of necessary fields.

title: Generalize drive_update()
description:
We will soon have `drive_update()` once #141 gets merged. 🎉

Right now it's hard-wired to do a media upload. What if you want to update metadata (alone or along with media update)?

title: drive_copy() needs to expose ...
description:
https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/reference/files/copy

For discussion: It should be possible to send those optional query parameters and to patch more of metadata via the body.

title: Add or remove multiple parent folders
description:
`drive_update()` does not seem happy to add or remove multiple parents at once. Example:

```
> file <- file %>%
+   drive_update(removeParents = c(
+     "0B0Gh-SuuA2nTZWZZRzhCZmNqOUU",
+     "0B0Gh-SuuA2nTVXYyQlowaktKUzQ"))
  Error in vapply(elements, encode, character(1)) : 
  values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[2]]) result is length 2 
```

Using `list()` vs `c()` does not help. This is not a common task but would be good to sort out.

title: CI errors for pull requests
description:
Our tests are now set up to skip auth-requiring tests when no token is available.

But builds associated with a pull request can still fail, because the unconditional attempt to decrypt the OAuth token will fail.

Case in point on AppVeyor (build is associated with a pull request):

https://ci.appveyor.com/project/tidyverse/googledrive/build/1.0.729

Note the same repo state leads to a passing build when it's regarded as a commit to a branch in the project):

https://ci.appveyor.com/project/tidyverse/googledrive/build/1.0.728

We need to figure out how to conditionally suppress the decrypt attempt on a PR or, in any case, don't let failure to decrypt cause actual failure.

Travis is not making this exact same mistake, but it might once we get a PR from someone who doesn't have push access.

title: create demos or articles of quirky use cases
description:
some I've thought of so far:
* ability to push slides made in RStudio to drive every time you render
* creating a "live" resume like [this](https://lucymcgowan.shinyapps.io/live-cv/) with Google Drive + shiny (or a semi-live one that just needs re-rendering like [this](http://www.lucymcgowan.com/html-cv/live-cv.html))
* storing an .rda file on Google drive & using it in an R analysis (like #17)
* collaborating on a .Rmd on Google Drive & rendering in R (tricky, because versioning...would work fine if it was only edited on the Google Drive, but hard to manage that)
* creating a document & adding a tibble of people by sending them an email (with glue!)

title: Helpers for working with q in drive_find()
description:
We need some internal support for q handling. I'll come back to flesh this out. Brain dump and notes from #7.

> Forming q. At its simplest, people have to provide q verbatim. But it might be nice to accept a vector of q's or multiple q's in ..., which `drive_list()` would then concatenate with "and". It feels like there's also a need for an internal "append this to q" helper.

How do we -- or do we -- reconcile defaults (such as “not being in trash”) with user’s supplied q and/or q clauses we build up? Re: user … should they be forced to declare whether their q should trump everything or be added to the defaults?

Do we attempt to pull user-supplied q apart into clauses? Have some clause-checking machinery, then “and” it all back together?

title: Update messages in confirm functions
description:
* Look into updating `confirm_single_file()` to allow for custom messages as mentioned in #112

> Perhaps that means we should improve the messaging in those checkers. Or allow a message to be provided in the call, so that you can override with something more informative, when possible and important?

title: Uniform handling of messages
description: We should work out some policies about messages, warning, and errors. Re: the form of the message and the mechanics of how we'll make them. There's lots of diversity right now.

title: Favor path over name in drive_cp(), drive_upload() & friends
description:
Our docs claim:
```
#' @param name Character, new file name if not specified as part of `path`. Any
#'   name obtained from `path` overrides this argument. Defaults to "Copy of
#'   {CURRENT-FILE-NAME}."
```
but the code seems to imply exactly the opposite 🤔:
``` 
 if (is_path(path)) {
    if (is.null(name) && drive_path_exists(append_slash(path))) {
      path <- append_slash(path)
    }
    path_parts <- partition_path(path, maybe_name = is.null(name))
    path <- path_parts$parent
    name <- name %||% path_parts$name
  }
```

- [x] This can likely be fixed by flipping the last line as so:
```
name <- path_parts$name %||% name
```
*edit: ended up changing the docs instead*
- [x] Add tests checking this behaves as expected

title: Allow `q` to be passed to `drive_get()`
description: This is currently needed so we can query the trash for `drive_untrash()`, but I can see other circumstances where we wish we could give a path and also pass something to the `q` parameter.

description:
Hi,

Thank you so much for this library. I'm currently using it for our project. I realized however, that as the changes are certainly greatly improving, I'd like to request if possible that you manage the releases better. title: Unify drive_get() and drive_path()
description: As it turns out, specifying file by id seems to be least common method (vs name/path and dribble). So let's have `drive_get(path, id)`.

title: Be able to report the path(s) for a file
description:
We might need a function that goes from file id to path(s). It's pretty close to what `get_paths()` already does.

Why do we need it? When naming a file in messages, we currently use just the name. But we're often in a context where user has specified input as path and the message will be much more interpretable if it also uses a path.

title: Delete vs put in trash
description:
I wonder if we should offer `drive_trash()` instead of `drive_delete()`.

And then have a function to empty the trash.

And `drive_untrash()` to pull something back out of the trash.

The browser UI makes it much harder to truly delete things than we currently do. I don't want to make it easy for people to shoot themselves in the foot.

title: Lower the minimum R version
description: at least to 3.2 or preferably 3.1

title: Built-in files
description:
Recording these for myself. Built-in files of disparate type that are handy for tests and examples.

```r
system.file("DESCRIPTION")
browseURL(R.home('doc/html/Rlogo.pdf'))
R.home('doc/html/Rlogo.svg')
browseURL(R.home('doc/html/logo.jpg'))
R.home('doc/BioC_mirrors.csv')  %>% readLines()

title: File identification
description:
We probably want to do some renaming. `drive_from_path()` and `drive_from_id()` better describe what the current `drive_path()` and `drive_get()` functions do. Too clunky though?

It also seems odd that those functions can't take a vector of inputs, but `as_dribble.character()` and `as_dribble.drive_id()` can. Think about this.

All the ways to identify files:

  * `drive_path()`
  * `drive_get()`
  * `drive_search()`
  * `drive_ls()`
  * `as_dribble()` on character vector and `drive_id` vector and (for internal use) list of Files Resource objects or `dribble`

The ones that start with `drive_` are conceived to be called directly by a user. `as_dribble()` is generally used internally to pre-process user input describing the file(s) to act on.

title: Re-wrangle stored info re: Drive API
description:

> You might want to consider a two-layer request builder, like here:
> https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets2/blob/8caf705a92b7c0638783ce478eb0449a3a92c1de/R/gs_build_request.R#L47

> The inner layer, gs_build_request(), is very dumb and mechanical. But would work if someone really knew what they were doing and only wanted help setting base URL, path param expansion, and managing auth.

> The outer layer, gs_generate_request(), is smarter and what I plan to use! It needs to be given a known endpoint and then it looks up everything we know, checks that input looks good, and massages it into shape before calling gs_build_request().

description:
I have a second generation solution for resolving a requested path, such as `foo/bar/baz`.

I'd like to look ahead a bit and package it more generally, i.e. for use beyond `drive_ls()`.

@LucyMcGowan Will you help me list the ways other functions will need to work with paths?

`drive_list()`: User can supply path. We need to make sure such a path exists and is uniquely defined. Then determine file id for the terminal leaf and list it.

Functions that create or move files: We need to determine the maximal existing stem, in case some folders need to be created. Example: user asks to write a file to `foo/bar/baz/yo/myfile.txt`. We determine that `foo/bar` exists and that we need to create `baz` within `foo/bar` and `yo` within `foo/bar/baz`.

What else do we need?

```
I see
```
## Error: The path 'test_8675309/foo/yo/' identifies more than one file:
## File of type folder, with id 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTOEVQX1BteW1Fa3M.
## File of type folder, with id 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTN3VMYWdOZlhrM0k.
```
but on drive I have:
test_8675309
+-- foo
| +-- yo (id 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTOEVQX1BteW1Fa3M)
+-- yo (id 0B0Gh-SuuA2nTN3VMYWdOZlhrM0k)

so in fact test_8675309/foo/yo should be unique (since the other one that it's fussing about is actually test_8675309/yo)

Also, when checking through the path, match [here](https://github.com/tidyverse/googledrive/blob/master/R/drive_path.R#L33) doesn't allow for nested folders with the same name. For example if we had "foo/foo", which is perfectly logical, match only matches the first, so we would have depth 1 for both, where they should each be listed as both depth 1 and 2.

title: Interface of drive_list()
description:
I think you should make heavy reference to `list.files()`. Specifically:

  * `path`: Should default to meaning "list my Drive files", which strikes me as the closest match for "current working directory". But then user should also be able to specify a *folder* here as well.
  * `pattern`: that's what the regex should be called, instead of `search`
  * I think `type` should possibly be elevated to an argument in the signature of `drive_ls()` itself, as opposed to getting mopped up in `...`.
  * Lots of the other args of `list.files()` are also worth considering. Good to ask yourself: is there is an obvious translation of this into the world of Drive?

In general, you need to think about how to help people craft searches. Obviously step one is simply to link to the [file searching guide](https://developers.google.com/drive/v3/web/search-parameters), as we've done. And to include some good examples. But this is an example of something that might be ripe for an add-in down the road.
